scope: canonical profile mode with legacy compatibility

verification.command: approved architecture and Phase 3 planning-contract review
verification.summary: The approved architecture and delivery plan require Resolve/Profile reuse, structured 409/503 semantics, pure workbench state, stale-response rejection and removal of frontend final-fact inference. The detailed plan splits those requirements into three bounded runtime Slices.

No placeholders, conflicting request shapes or silent compatibility breaks remain. Slice 3A has exact files, red tests, orchestration signatures, HTTP mapping, local profiles, candidate SLO/40-spec proof, rollback and non-goals.

TDD produced the shared revision projection, one-query resolver authoring context, injectable runtime orchestration, structured Resolve route and canonical profile mode. After the first candidate exposed the real systemd direct-start import boundary, a subprocess regression test reproduced it and the focused domain suite passed 106 tests; the related orchestration/backend/facade/store suite passed 744 tests; package and direct runtime imports and modules compiled.
1177 Python tests passed with 1 skipped, compileall passed and the Strict Harness check passed.
365 Node tests and 1177 Python tests passed with 1 skipped; all 127 JSON, syntax, Harness and diff commands passed.

No unresolved critical or important findings. Review caught and fixed two trust-boundary defects with red-to-green tests: an independent resolver-context revision-query exception could discard an otherwise valid public gear payload, and the dormant facade could report a canonical profile resolved without executable talents. Optional authoring context is now isolated, while canonical profile readiness requires a non-empty profile, executable talent encoding and server-owned gear readiness; blocked output clears the profile and marks readiness false. Review also confirmed one selected-gear PostgreSQL boundary, unchanged pure Resolver/Ledger ownership, real 400/409/503 mapping, legacy profile compatibility, and no migration, write, sync, Worker, frontend, Phase 4 Manifest or Catalyst activation.

verification.command: second candidate 40-spec hard gate and corrected remote PostgreSQL read-only preflight
verification.summary: The second candidate started cleanly but the real 40-spec gate passed only 3/40, so it was rolled back. Exact problem evidence exposed four authority gaps: class armor restrictions were applied to cloak/shield slots, Fury dual_wield_2h was collapsed into ordinary dual-wield rules, ranged main hand did not occupy off hand for readiness, and semantically identical raw/normalized variant rows were treated as conflicting aliases. Eleven focused red-to-green cases now keep missing rule parameters and semantically divergent aliases fail-closed. The corrected code passed 112 domain tests and 744 related backend/store/facade/orchestration tests, then a temporary remote read-only preflight against the live public templates and PostgreSQL authority resolved 40/40 with zero failures (18 fifteen-slot and 22 sixteen-slot Intents); the temporary tree was removed.

verification.command: local CR of live-authority correction at 827fcf0
verification.summary: No unresolved critical or important findings. Armor restriction remains an explicit backend-owned slot parameter and fails closed when absent; two-hand dual-wield is allowed only for the exact dual_wield_2h mode; ranged and ordinary two-hand occupancy remain distinct; public alias duplicates merge only when every semantic field matches and preserve all evidence refs, while divergent rows remain unavailable. Resolver/Ledger stay pure, PostgreSQL reads stay bounded and read-only, and no public template, migration, write, sync, frontend or Catalyst behavior was activated.

verification.command: third candidate failure capture and exact rollback at e81976d
verification.summary: The corrected candidate passed 40/40 public Resolve, the 11-spec verified-talent Profile matrix, truthful blocking for 29 specs without verified talent imports, and malformed/stale/wrong-slot/missing-authority negative HTTP. It failed the performance hard gate: cold p95 was 398.046ms, warm p95 was 429.227ms against the 200ms limit, and the functionally correct 20x5 burst reached p95 5161.417ms. The route created a new PostgresCacheStore per request, so its bounded AuthorityContextCache never produced a warm hit. The candidate was immediately rolled back to exact Phase 2B; TDD now shares only the DSN-isolated Authority LRU across request-scoped stores and makes the LRU thread-safe without sharing connections or the store's unrelated raw catalog cache.

verification.command: TDD cache-scope correction and fresh local verification at 9be919b
verification.summary: Red tests reproduced the request-scoped cache miss and absent LRU synchronization. The correction shares one 32-entry/4 MiB Authority cache for the current hashed PostgreSQL DSN, replaces it on configuration change or disabled PG runtime, keeps stores and connections request-scoped, and protects LRU ordering and byte accounting with an RLock. Focused cache/store/backend tests passed, 114 domain/runtime tests passed, 734 related backend/store/API tests passed, the backend profile passed 1190 Python tests with 1 skipped, and the full profile passed 365 Node plus 1190 Python tests with 1 skipped and all 127 commands. Local CR found no unresolved critical or important issue.
